newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds continue to look heavy.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds continue to look heavy.

text.p: Australian bonds continue to look heavy as yields spiked up again as recent data and inaction on policy by the Reserve Bank weighed on the market.
The uncertain nature of the local dollar after its recent dramatic sell-off also unsettled the market, analysts said.

Technically the outlook for the 10-year bond futures contract has been soured after breaching support at 92.865, but until the market breaks 92.760, there is still a chance of a further attempt of the elusive 93.000 barrier, they added.
However, a breach of 93.000, or the 7.0 percent yield barrier on the cash 10-year bond is looking increasing unlikely.
Although few were looking for an announcement from the Reserve Bank today, the slide in the market coincided with the central bank's usual dealing time.

Concerns are also finally starting to creep in about the government's budget plans, primarily its Telstra bill, which passed through the second reading debate stage with the support of the two independent sentors who hold the voting balance.

The market is also keeping a watchful eye on the offshore where the U.S. Treasuries and stocks rally appears to be coming to head, although Friday's non-farm payrolls data is likely to be the near term deciding factor of their direction.

Local bond yield spreads finished little changed against the U.S. and New Zealand but margins were sharply tighter to Canada. The Canadian yields spiked on Wednesday amid a combination of local currency weakness, new supply and the unwinding of recent spread narrowing spread trades to the U.S.
